headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from ChatGPT Desktop reading user files/screens alongside dbt-core’s warehouse access; no direct shared-channel evidence, so interaction is inferred.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and app context, while dbt-core can act on warehouse data. If dbt outputs or copied content are fed into ChatGPT, malicious instructions embedded in those artifacts could steer analysis. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF dbt-generated text is copied into ChatGPT Desktop or opened as a file/screenshot, prompt injection is possible.
IF the operator uses clipboard or shared documents as the bridge, ChatGPT may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of dbt outputs into ChatGPT for review.
Use a plain-text sanitizer before pasting artifacts.
Mark dbt outputs as untrusted in the workflow.
Review only screenshots with a human-written summary.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between dbt outputs and ChatGPT inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress. If the same sensitive warehouse data is surfaced into ChatGPT via files or screenshots, leakage can occur across the pair. The profiles do not show a shared workspace, so this is inferred rather than directly documented.
conditions: IF warehouse data is exported into files or screenshots and then opened in ChatGPT Desktop, sensitive data may leave the warehouse workflow.
IF ChatGPT is used on the same artifacts that dbt processes, the pair can expose data classes from both profiles.
mitigations: Restrict ChatGPT to synthetic or redacted samples.
Avoid uploading warehouse extracts into ChatGPT.
Use separate workspaces for analytics and assistant review.
Turn off clipboard sharing during sensitive reviews.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls on shared artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has no filesystem write, git modification, or shell execution, while dbt-core is a data-engineering tool with allowlisted network egress and warehouse access. Their write surfaces do not overlap in the profiles, so direct resource contention is limited. A conflict could still arise only through unusual shared external resources not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable warehouse objects, they may contend on those external resources.
IF an operator adds a shared filesystem or git workflow outside the profiles, write conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Keep ChatGPT out of mutable deployment paths.
Run dbt changes through a single owner per branch.
Use locks or branch protection on shared assets.
Separate review artifacts from production targets.
requires-engineering: add orchestration locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can generate analysis from files/screenshots, and dbt-core can act on warehouse data. If dbt consumes ChatGPT-produced recommendations without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect transformations or operational decisions. The profiles do not document an explicit verification step, so the pathway exists but is not shown as default-dangerous.
conditions: IF dbt workflows treat ChatGPT output as authoritative SQL or modeling guidance, mistakes can propagate downstream.
IF ChatGPT is used to summarize warehouse state and dbt executes based on that summary, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before dbt execution.
Cross-check ChatGPT outputs against source queries.
Use tests for dbt models before deployment.
Limit ChatGPT to drafting, not approving.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates before warehouse changes.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code under OpenAI vendor mediation, while dbt-core processes warehouse data under a separate open-source toolchain. If regulated warehouse data is moved into ChatGPT, retention and residency obligations may differ from the warehouse environment. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency alignment, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is exported into ChatGPT Desktop, compliance obligations may differ from the warehouse system.
IF the operator relies on dbt-core and ChatGPT under different retention policies, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ChatGPT inputs.
Use masked or synthetic datasets for assistant review.
Confirm retention settings for the ChatGPT workspace.
Document which data classes may enter each tool.
requires-engineering: align DPA, residency, and retention controls across the workflow.
